items.title: Is incrementalism enough in a systems-change world?
items.summary: Here’s a question that’s been keeping me up at night: Are sustainability professionals — all of us, individually and collectively — working at the wrong level?

items.title: Report: Global battery energy storage set to grow six-fold by 2030
items.summary: To support ongoing renewables expansion, the battery energy storage market is expected to grow six-fold worldwide by the end of the decade, with China and the US leading the charge.

items.title: How are tighter budgets reshaping the sustainability profession?
items.summary: The sustainability profession is entering a period of change as organisations rethink how dedicated sustainability functions are structured and funded, new research suggests.

items.title: Virgin Media O2 launches interactive pilot to encourage tech reuse
items.summary: Virgin Media O2 is piloting the ‘O2 Tech Refab Lab’ at its flagship Westfield Stratford City store, featuring discovery zones where customers can learn how devices can receive a second life.

items.title: NGOs call on PM to tackle inequality amid North Sea drilling rumours
items.summary: Almost 100 charity leaders, including from Oxfam, ActionAid and WaterAid, have urged Prime Minister (PM) Andy Burnham to help address the root causes of poverty, including climate change.

items.title: Getting ahead: Five ways to future-proof supply chains
items.summary: From climate shocks and water scarcity to geopolitical tensions and resource constraints, supply chain disruption has become a defining business risk.

items.title: Fossil fuel giants to double profits as emissions spike, research finds
items.summary: Fossil fuel firms including BP, Chevron, and Shell are expected to double their combined net income to $45bn this quarter, with research stating that emissions from the world’s largest oil and gas businesses were sufficient to cause one quarter of heatwaves experienced in the last 20 years.

items.title: Analysis: Wind and solar power overtake fossil fuels in Germany for first time ever
items.summary: More of Germany’s electricity came from wind and solar power than fossil fuels for the first time ever in 2025.

items.title: Analysis: 84% of nations miss deadline to identify ‘nature-harming’ subsidies by 2025
items.summary: Most countries failed to meet a 2025 target to identify all of their subsidies that could be “harmful” to biodiversity, according to Carbon Brief analysis.
